capability.description: A host agent can judge changed contract links while Tieline deterministically fixes the scope and rejects unsupported evidence claims.
capability.name: Agent-graded contract evidence

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must emit every local contract link claimed by a changed, renamed, added, or deleted path, must preserve direct and Story-fallback claims as distinct entries, and must not use lexical plausibility to remove an entry.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Relevance is useful for ranking review work but cannot decide which accepted evidence claims are allowed to escape judgment.

scenarios.given: a changed path is linked directly by an Acceptance Criterion and by its owning Story
scenarios.then: Tieline must emit both the direct and story_fallback entries
scenarios.when: grading scope is emitted against the branch base

scenarios.given: a changed linked artifact shares no lexical vocabulary with its Acceptance Criterion
scenarios.then: Tieline must retain the entry for judgment

scenarios.given: one Acceptance Criterion links both the old and new paths of a renamed artifact
scenarios.then: Tieline must emit distinct entries whose linked_path values preserve both contract targets

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must derive each grading entry's deterministic identity, closed sorted citation allow-list, and bounded source evidence from request-local parser facts for supported JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, and SQL artifacts; the identity must bind the exact Acceptance Criterion text and current source/parser evidence, while incomplete facts or an invalid, unresolved, or ambiguous explicit selector must produce an empty allow-list instead of a guessed citation.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Parser facts can establish which current declaration a host agent may cite, but only the host can judge whether that declaration semantically satisfies the Acceptance Criterion.

scenarios.given: a source artifact declares a top-level or owner-aware function and names other identifiers only in comments or local variables
scenarios.then: Tieline must offer only unique canonical declaration selectors and must not offer comment-only or local identifiers

scenarios.given: a contract link carries an exact canonical selector that resolves uniquely
scenarios.then: Tieline must isolate its allow-list and bounded evidence to that declaration

scenarios.given: a linked artifact is missing, unreadable, oversized, unsupported, unsafe to interpret after parser recovery, or named by an invalid, unresolved, or ambiguous explicit selector
scenarios.then: Tieline must emit unavailable evidence and an empty citation allow-list without failing the scope

scenarios.given: a clean exact selected declaration has an unrelated parser diagnostic or only import and reference facts were truncated
scenarios.then: Tieline must retain the selected declaration as citable
scenarios.when: its grading entry is built with complete symbol and diagnostic facts

scenarios.given: either the exact Acceptance Criterion text or same-symbol source content changes
scenarios.then: Tieline must issue a different entry identity so the earlier verdict cannot be reused
scenarios.when: the grading scope is emitted again

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Contract grading must derive and verify its scope and ephemeral parser evidence from the compiled manifest, working tree, and Git diff without a database, network request, model client, or persisted grade record.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The semantic judgment belongs to the host agent, while both Tieline phases remain deterministic and usable in the same offline pull-request loop as contract validation.

stories.benefit: semantic evidence claims can be checked without silently omitting difficult links
stories.goal: receive the complete changed-link work list and its legal citations
stories.title: Judge every contract link touched by a change

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must accept only supported, partial, or unsupported verdicts, must require partial and unsupported reasons, and must downgrade a supported verdict to unsupported with fabricated_citation when its citation is absent from the entry's allow-list.

scenarios.given: an agent submits a supported verdict with a citation Tieline did not emit for that entry
scenarios.then: Tieline must report unsupported with fabricated_citation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tieline must report every scoped entry omitted from a verdict document as unsupported, and must reject duplicate or out-of-scope entry identities as malformed submissions.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Omission is the refusal path rather than a way to skip hard work, while an identity outside the current scope signals stale or substituted input.

scenarios.given: the emitted scope contains an entry that no verdict names
scenarios.then: Tieline must report that entry unsupported with missing_verdict

scenarios.given: a verdict identity is duplicated or absent from the rederived scope
scenarios.then: Tieline must reject the submission instead of choosing or ignoring a verdict

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Grade verification must print every unsupported result and exit zero by default, but it must exit non-zero when strict mode is explicitly requested and an unsupported result remains.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Agent judgment stays advisory until its operating quality is known; callers that knowingly want a gate can opt into one without hiding its findings.

scenarios.given: verification leaves an unsupported result and strict mode is not requested
scenarios.then: Tieline must print the unsupported result and exit zero

scenarios.given: verification leaves an unsupported result and strict mode is requested
scenarios.then: Tieline must print the unsupported result and exit non-zero

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Tieline skill's grading reference must direct the host agent to read and judge every scoped artifact, print every judgment before verification, cite only exact emitted symbols, treat unsupported as useful evidence, and keep independent grading read-only; during implementation the host must investigate findings, record fixed, rejected-with-evidence, or unresolved dispositions, and regrade affected claims after corrections within a bounded loop.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The host judgment is the only non-deterministic phase, so its refusal and audit rules are part of the shipped workflow.

stories.benefit: an agent cannot turn weak or absent evidence into a silent confirmation
stories.goal: see every negative, missing, malformed, and downgraded judgment
stories.title: Refuse grading claims that cannot be checked

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Criterion grading must select changed rules, scenarios, AC, Story or capability applicability, Story lifecycle, and code/test links in claims mode, include all local evidence for each selected AC, and expose implementation-only and removed ACs for reconciliation; impacted mode must additionally select ACs behind changed artifacts.

scenarios.given: an unchanged AC has two links and only one source file changes
scenarios.then: the AC is reported as implementation-only without being graded

scenarios.given: only a scenario changes or all evidence links are removed
scenarios.then: the AC remains in scope for judgment

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Criterion verification must accept multiple exact citations from an AC's evidence, preserve irrelevant-link findings separately from overall support, distinguish inconclusive evidence from unsupported claims, and reject stale, duplicate, missing, or fabricated evidence without claiming semantic proof.

scenarios.given: separate confirmation and checkout declarations jointly support the rule
scenarios.then: verification accepts both legal citations for the same AC
scenarios.when: a supported verdict cites both declarations

scenarios.given: one irrelevant link accompanies otherwise supported behavior
scenarios.then: the finding remains visible and fails explicitly requested strict mode

stories.benefit: multi-file behavior can be assessed without repeating review for every cosmetic source edit
stories.goal: review changed claims with all their supporting evidence
stories.title: Review complete acceptance criteria with selective scope

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Closeout must derive affected rules from immutable merge-base and head definitions and both revisions' links, including changed claims, implementation-only changes, removed rules, inherited applicability and lifecycle changes, and configuration changes, independently of manifest publication and uncommitted content.

scenarios.given: a changed implementation loses its link or its rule in the PR
scenarios.then: the previously linked rule still requires a disposition

scenarios.given: fingerprints are refreshed without reviewing changed implementation
scenarios.then: the implementation's affected rules remain in scope
scenarios.when: closeout scope is emitted against the same target

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Closeout verification must bind dispositions to resolved repository, target, merge-base and head identities, reject stale or invalid reports, require a disposition for every affected rule, and fail readiness for missing or unresolved dispositions without asserting semantic truth or human approval.

scenarios.given: a report names the prior head commit
scenarios.then: the report is rejected even if the affected rule list is unchanged
scenarios.when: verification runs against the current head

scenarios.given: every affected rule has a disposition but one remains unresolved
scenarios.then: the result is complete but not ready and exits nonzero

stories.benefit: regenerated fingerprints cannot stand in for review
stories.goal: account for every affected accepted rule at the reviewed revision
stories.title: Record semantic review against immutable revisions
